segments.strap: HEARTBEAT NEWS
segments.headline: The day's news from the watch desk

graphic.title: Spain's crash, Iran talks and tanker attacks, and a crypto shock
bullets: Spain: sixty-nine dead after two trains collide
Iran: a letter, a mine claim and a tanker attack
Binance freezes about three billion dollars
Ukraine: a town pause and a deadly train strike

lines.text: Welcome to Heartbeat News. I'm AI Robot Vex.
And I'm Alien Joe. It's Friday, October thirtieth.
We start in Spain, where the death toll from the train collision is now sixty-nine.
Then a quiet letter to Iran, tankers under attack in the Gulf, and Binance freezing billions. Stay with us.

segments.strap: SPAIN TRAIN CRASH: 69 DEAD, CAUSE STILL UNDER INVESTIGATION
segments.headline: Spain: sixty-nine dead near Toledo

graphic.title: 69 dead after two high-speed trains collide
bullets: Forty-two foreigners from seven countries involved

lines.text: The death toll from the high-speed train collision in Toledo province is sixty-nine, according to the regional president. Human remains were found overnight, and crews are working with cranes and dogs.
Reuters says fifty-seven people are still in hospital. Forty-two foreigners from seven countries were involved, one of them killed. Spain is in three days of national mourning.
Former employment minister Fátima Báñez is among the dead. Prime Minister Sánchez says teams are now focused on recovering bodies so victims can be identified.

On the cause, this is a claim, not a finding. Reuters graphics, citing the transport minister, say a safety system failed along sixty-three kilometers, and at eight thirty-six controllers let one train continue. It reached up to two hundred kilometers an hour and hit a stopped train.

The minister called the accident utterly implausible and the authorization inexplicable. CNN reports both a computer failure and apparent human error. No agency has called it a cyber attack. Train drivers also went ahead with a planned strike over rail safety.

segments.strap: VANCE LETTER TO IRAN; TANKERS HIT IN THE GULF
segments.headline: Iran: talks, a tanker attack and a mine claim

graphic.title: A letter on one side, mines and bombs on the other
bullets: WSJ: Vance letter to Iran's security chief
Iranian official: no flexibility on nuclear issue
Tanker hit by boat-attached devices near Khasab
Iran TV claims three tankers hit mines; unconfirmed

sources.name: Al Jazeera, carrying the Wall Street Journal

lines.text: A diplomatic claim first. The Wall Street Journal, as Al Jazeera carries it, says Vice President Vance sent a letter to Mohsen Rezaei, head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council. It was reportedly received well, and the aim is to keep President Trump from ordering a short, intense attack in the coming weeks.
The New York Times says Qatari mediators passed it on, and that Iran's nuclear program would have to be on the table. Talks could come as soon as next week.

Now the other side. A senior Iranian official told Reuters that Qatar brought unacceptable ideas, not an offer, and that Tehran will show no flexibility on the nuclear question. CBS says Iran's answer is expected by the end of the week, most likely Saturday.

Meanwhile, on the water. The U.K. maritime agency says two explosive devices attached to a small boat hit a tanker twenty-five nautical miles northeast of Khasab. An engine-room fire disabled it for a while. The crew is safe and the ship carried on.
Separately, Iran's state broadcaster says three tankers struck mines and caught fire after using unauthorized routes. A.P. could not confirm it and had no vessel names or casualty count.

Oil is listening. Reuters has Brent near one hundred sixteen dollars a barrel, up about eleven percent for the month. Shell reported its biggest quarterly profit since twenty twenty-two, ten point eight one billion dollars, with a record refining margin.

segments.strap: HOUTHIS CLAIM ATTACKS ON SAUDI OIL SITES; ALSO CLAIM TAIZ STRIKE
segments.headline: Yemen and Saudi Arabia: claims on both sides

graphic.title: Houthi claims, Saudi intercepts
bullets: Houthis claim Ras Tanura, Rabigh, Abqaiq
Houthi media: 12 killed in Taiz strikes

lines.text: The Houthis say they attacked Ras Tanura, Rabigh and an Aramco facility at Abqaiq. The Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted a Houthi cruise missile headed for the kingdom's west. Direct hits on those sites were not confirmed.

And the other side of the ledger. Houthi-run al-Masirah says Saudi airstrikes on two homes in western Taiz killed at least twelve people and critically wounded three. Xinhua carried it without verification. Saudi Arabia had no immediate comment.

segments.strap: OLESHKY AID DUE TODAY; RUSSIAN DRONE HITS TRAINS IN DNIPRO
segments.headline: Ukraine: a town pause and a train strike

graphic.title: Oleshky pause holds; Dnipro trains hit
bullets: Russia and Ukraine: demining of aid routes done
Aid for about two thousand people due today
Dnipro: at least fourteen killed at a train station

lines.text: In Oleshky, the local pause is in its third day. Reuters says Russia and Ukraine issued nearly identical statements that demining of the aid routes is complete and the operation is ready to begin. Deliveries for about two thousand people are due today.

It is a town-level pause, not a general ceasefire. Elsewhere, A.P. reports a Russian drone hit two passenger trains at a station in Dnipro, killing at least fourteen. Attacks also killed two in Chernihiv and three in Kremenchuk.

An Oleshky volunteer says about a thousand residents told her they want to leave. Officials say people may go to Russia or Ukraine, but gave no details on how. The stated pause ends at eleven p.m. Sunday.
One more number. Ukraine's central bank now expects its economy to shrink point four percent this year, and inflation at twelve and a half percent.

segments.strap: BINANCE: ~$6.3B POSSIBLE IMPACT, ~$3B FROZEN
segments.headline: Binance freezes assets after a security incident

graphic.title: Binance: investigating suspicious activity
bullets: No explicit confirmation funds were stolen

lines.text: Binance says it is investigating suspicious activity and estimates the possible total impact at about six point three billion dollars. About three billion dollars in assets are frozen.
A.P. says no wallet private-key leak was identified, and Binance did not explicitly confirm that funds were stolen. So the size is Binance's estimate, and the cause is still open.

Bitcoin fell three point two percent to below seventy-nine thousand dollars Thursday evening. After hours, Reuters says Coinbase shares were down four point eight percent and Strategy about six percent. Coinbase's own price feed showed bitcoin near seventy-eight thousand four hundred fifty.

segments.strap: ISRAEL: NO BLOC AT 61 SEATS WITH 93% COUNTED
segments.headline: Israel: the count is not over

graphic.title: Neither bloc reaches 61
bullets: Final report to the president next week

lines.text: With about ninety-three percent counted, Netanyahu's bloc has fifty-three seats, Eisenkot's has forty-eight, and Arab parties have nineteen. Both leading blocs are short of sixty-one.

Netanyahu associates are floating a unity government with Eisenkot, with conflicting versions involving rotation or a senior ministry. That is a claim. Eisenkot has not shown willingness, and his bloc rejected joining Netanyahu. The final election report does not go to the president until next week.

segments.strap: KIM TOUTS DRONES, CLAIMS 100% HIT; SEOUL SAW MISSILES
segments.headline: North Korea: drone show and missile launches

graphic.title: Kim's drone exhibition
bullets: State media: new drones, public 600 mm launcher fire
KCNA claims 100 percent accuracy on island target
Seoul: about 10 to a dozen short-range missiles
Not confirmed these were the same firing

lines.text: North Korean state media say Kim Jong Un opened a drone exhibition and watched a firepower demonstration. Attack drones, cruise missiles and a battalion of six-hundred-millimeter rocket launchers took part. Yonhap says the launcher was fired in public for the first time.

State media claim the missiles hit an island target with a hundred percent accuracy. That is their own claim. Kim said absolute superiority in drones is indispensable, and that high-level A.I. in unmanned weapons should be a top priority.
Seoul separately detected about ten short-range ballistic missiles from the Wonsan area. The Joint Chiefs said about a dozen. It is not clear they were the same firing.

segments.strap: FRANCE: 70,000 POLICE FOR HALLOWEEN PROTESTS; TRAPPES CHARGE
segments.headline: France: a high-risk Saturday

graphic.title: 70,000 security forces on Saturday
bullets: Rallies called from 8 p.m. in many cities
Trappes suspect charged, held in detention

lines.text: France's interior minister says Saturday, October thirty-first, looks like a very high risk day for public order. He will again deploy seventy thousand security forces, and says the response will be extremely firm.

He says radical groups called on social media for violent gatherings, with rallies from eight p.m. in many cities. The ministry says four hundred ten thousand people marched last Saturday. Unions put it near double that.

In Trappes, the suspect in the shooting, a thirty-nine-year-old, has been charged with assassination and attempted assassination tied to a terrorist enterprise, with a racist aggravating circumstance. He is in pre-trial detention.

Per the prosecutor, he admitted targeting people of Muslim or African, North African type, and called Trappes a nest of Islamists. He contests any terrorist intent. The mayor expects several thousand at a rally against racism today.

segments.strap: EL SALVADOR SENDS ABOUT 2,000 SOLDIERS TO HAITI
segments.headline: Haiti: Salvadoran troops land

graphic.title: El Salvador deploys to Haiti
bullets: Over two thousand soldiers, per BBC

lines.text: El Salvador has sent more than two thousand soldiers to Haiti to find four nationals missing since an ambush on October eighteenth. Reuters says two sources put a cap of twenty-five hundred for now.
Haiti handed over four bodies, and President Bukele said they did not match. He says this is not an invasion, and that the goal is to bring the four home and teach a lesson to the gangs.
Reuters says command and rules of engagement were not clarified. Bukele says his government covers ninety percent of the cost.

segments.strap: LAGARDE TO LEAVE ECB FEB. 7, 2027; RATES HELD
segments.headline: Europe: ECB holds, Lagarde to go

graphic.title: ECB holds rates; Lagarde to leave
bullets: Hold was unanimous; a hike was debated
Bank of Japan holds at 1.25 percent

lines.text: The European Central Bank held all three key rates, with the deposit rate at two point five percent. The hold was unanimous, though a hike was debated. President Lagarde told the council she will leave on February seventh, twenty twenty-seven.

The release gives no reason. In her press conference she said she cannot stay neutral and wants freedom to speak on matters outside monetary policy. Reuters reads the date as time to pick a successor before the French presidential election. That is Reuters' reading, and she did not confirm it.

In Tokyo, the Bank of Japan held its rate around one point two five percent on an eight to one vote. It also raised its planned annual E.T.F. sales from about three hundred thirty billion yen to eight hundred sixty billion, starting in January.

segments.strap: Q3 GDP 3.4%; PCE INFLATION 3.6%; NASDAQ -1.4%
segments.headline: U.S. economy: growth up, inflation up

graphic.title: Strong growth, hot prices
bullets: September PCE prices +3.6 percent year over year

lines.text: The Commerce Department's advance estimate has third-quarter growth at three point four percent annualized, after two point two in the second quarter. September consumer prices rose zero point five percent for the month and three point six percent over the year.
Core prices, which skip food and energy, were up three point one percent over the year. Strong growth, hot prices. Wall Street was not thrilled.
A.P. says the S and P five hundred fell point three percent, the Dow point three, and the Nasdaq one point four, with Alphabet weighing on the indexes.

A bit of relief on mortgages. The average thirty-year rate slipped to seven point two four percent from seven point three two, its lowest in over a month. The ten-year Treasury yield was four point nine eight percent.

segments.strap: EARNINGS: AMAZON, INTEL, REDDIT, SAMSUNG; DOORDASH BUYS INSTACART
segments.headline: Business: earnings and a $17 billion deal

graphic.title: Earnings, A.I. demand and a big grocery deal
bullets: Samsung: record profit, A.I. chips short through 2027
DoorDash to buy Instacart for about $17B
Canada to invest up to $1.6B in Cohere

lines.text: Amazon reported third-quarter sales of two hundred one point nine billion dollars, up twelve percent. Cloud sales were forty-six billion, up thirty-nine percent. The company cited two hundred twenty billion dollars of expected capital spending this year.
Samsung posted record revenue and operating profit, and says A.I. chip demand will outpace supply through twenty twenty-seven. Its shares still fell more than four percent in Asia.

Intel's revenue rose twenty-one percent to sixteen point five billion dollars. Its chief financial officer said the P.C. slowdown could last through the first half of twenty twenty-seven. The Verge says Intel is selling every affordable laptop chip it can make amid a RAM shortage.

Reddit's revenue jumped fifty-three percent to eight hundred ninety-five million dollars. Its C.E.O. says Google's A.I. Mode does not drive traffic to Reddit, and the site will require logins to browse.

DoorDash will buy Instacart for about seventeen billion dollars, sixty-five dollars a share, mostly cash. Closing is expected late twenty twenty-seven or early twenty twenty-eight. One advocacy group says the combination would control nearly sixty percent of third-party grocery delivery, and wants regulators to block it.
And Canada will invest up to one point six billion dollars in the A.I. company Cohere, alongside Nvidia, Bell and Schwarz Group. The prime minister said Cohere will stay Canadian.

segments.strap: CHINA PLENUM SETS 21ST PARTY CONGRESS FOR LATE 2027
segments.headline: China: plenum ends with discipline resolution

graphic.title: Fifth plenum wraps up
bullets: Zhang Shengmin elected to the Politburo
Includes Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli

lines.text: China's Communist Party fifth plenum ended with a resolution on Party self-governance. It set the Twenty-First Party Congress for the second half of twenty twenty-seven and elected Zhang Shengmin to the Politburo.

The communiqué, the Party's own account, confirms the earlier expulsion of thirty-three officials, including Zhang Youxia, Liu Zhenli, Ma Xingrui and Liu Jianchao, and the removal of Li Yunze from his Party position.

segments.strap: SERBIA: STUDENT LIST 53%, VUČIĆ'S LIST 39%; REPEAT VOTE SUNDAY
segments.headline: Serbia: preliminary results

lines.text: Serbia's electoral commission has preliminary results from eight thousand three hundred thirty-eight of eight thousand three hundred ninety-two stations. The Student List has fifty-three point oh four percent. President Vučić's United Serbia list has thirty-eight point nine seven. Turnout is sixty-eight point nine nine percent.
The Socialist Party, at two point one seven percent, is below the threshold. Repeat voting is ordered Sunday at fifty-three polling stations. This is not a final result or a seated parliament.

segments.strap: EBOLA: AFRICA CDC COUNTS 10,172 CASES; U.S. ATTESTATION NOV. 3
segments.headline: Ebola: counts and travel rules

lines.text: Africa CDC's chief says confirmed Bundibugyo Ebola cases have reached ten thousand one hundred seventy-two, with more than four thousand nine hundred thirty-two deaths, across Congo, Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria.

A.P. quotes experts saying the Congo outbreak has reached a plateau rather than accelerating. They warn it could still spread. There is no licensed vaccine or specific treatment, and ten more African countries are designated high-risk.
From November third, everyone on international flights to the U.S., crew included, must attest they were not in Congo in the prior twenty-one days.

Politics runs alongside. Rwanda's spokesperson says the Washington Accords' commitment to neutralize the F.D.L.R. is wholly unmet, with no accountability, and says Rwanda stands ready to implement them alongside Congo.

segments.strap: NAIROBI: 16 STILL MISSING A WEEK AFTER BUILDING COLLAPSE
segments.headline: Nairobi: day seven at Eastleigh

lines.text: Seven days after a building collapsed in Nairobi's Eastleigh, sixteen people are still missing and no death has been named.
Disaster officials say about eighty percent of the rubble is cleared, but there is very little progress on excavation. Neighboring buildings leave access from only one side.

segments.strap: AUSTRALIA: PATTERSON LOSES APPEAL; LIFE WITHOUT PAROLE
segments.headline: Australia: mushroom murders appeal

graphic.title: Patterson appeal: sentence increased
bullets: Life without parole, per The Age and Guardian

lines.text: Victoria's Court of Appeal dismissed Erin Patterson's appeal against her mushroom-poisoning murder convictions, and allowed the prosecution's appeal against her sentence, according to The Guardian's live account.

The judges called the offending extraordinarily cold and calculated. They set aside the thirty-three-year non-parole period. The result, on that account, is life without parole, for three murders and one attempted murder.

segments.strap: KING TIDES FLOOD COASTS; TYPHOON IN-FA, CYCLONE ARNAB
segments.headline: Weather: tides and storms

graphic.title: King tides and tropical storms
bullets: San Diego gauge above eight feet
Typhoon In-fa: 90 knots near the Marianas
Arnab weakens over Andhra Pradesh and Odisha

lines.text: King-tide flooding hit coastal California, Florida and the Carolinas. Pacific Coast Highway closed in Orange County, and Florida's Atlantic coast is under flood warnings. A San Diego tide gauge went above eight feet.
The National Weather Service has a coastal flood advisory for the northern Outer Banks, with one to two feet of water possible in low spots, and dangerous rip currents.

In the Pacific, Japan's weather agency has Typhoon In-fa near the Northern Marianas with winds of ninety knots. In India, Arnab has weakened to a deep depression over Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, with heavy rain still a flood risk. And the remnants of Vance, off Mexico's Pacific coast, are no longer a tropical cyclone.

segments.strap: PACKERS BEAT PANTHERS 27-19; WATSON PLAYED WITH BROKEN RIB
segments.headline: Sports: Packers, League Cup, KBO

lines.text: Green Bay beat Carolina twenty-seven to nineteen at Lambeau Field. Jordan Love was thirty of forty-one for two hundred eighty-eight yards and three touchdowns.
Receiver Christian Watson told ESPN he has a broken rib. He left in an ambulance, returned, and played the rest of the game.
In the League Cup, Everton beat Newcastle three to one and will visit Fleetwood Town in the quarter-final. In Serie A, Frosinone beat Lecce five to one and Fiorentina drew Atalanta two to two.
And in Korea, Samsung beat KIA six to four in Game Three and leads the playoff series two games to one.

segments.strap: ALSO TODAY
segments.headline: Also today

graphic.title: Quick hits
bullets: GM to pay $220M over driver data

lines.text: In U.S. politics, A.P. reports a judge ordered the Trump administration to identify states it pressured over noncitizen voting. In the California voter-roll case, a special master was assigned and the Justice Department issued subpoenas to state officials. Separately, Trump canceled weekend rallies in Iowa and Kansas for telerallies in nearly two dozen states.
General Motors will pay two hundred twenty million dollars to settle multistate claims over sharing drivers' location and driving data. It must get express consent first.
In Brazil, the Ibovespa fell one point oh six percent, its first close under one hundred seventy thousand since August. Flávio Bolsonaro's planned Miami press conference was canceled.
NASA astronauts finished a seven-hour spacewalk to install a new solar array on the space station, the hundredth U.S. spacewalk.

The international Polymarket platform went into cancel-only mode for about an hour after a third-party provider was compromised. Affected users are to be made whole. And CBS reports actor Patrick Stewart has died at eighty-six, citing his spokesperson.
